newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU considering wheat tax cut - Commission sources.
newsitem.headline: EU considering wheat tax cut - Commission sources.

text.p: The European Union was considering a further cut in its wheat export taxes following lower domestic prices and prospects of another big crop, European Commission sources said on Thursday.
"It's being considered, the feeling is that there could be a reduction," said one source.

A cut in the taxes, or eliminating them altoether, would ease a source of friction with the United States ahead of talks in Washington on June 16 between EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler and U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman.
The U.S. says that export taxes, like subsidies, distort trade.
The EU imposed taxes on daily exports of wheat on April 24 in order to rein in prices and ensure adequate domestic supplies until the new harvest is gathered.
On May 29, it cut taxes on daily soft wheat grain exports to five Ecus a tonne from 15 Ecus, and on flour exports to seven Ecus a tonne from 20.
France's cereals authority, ONIC, says the wheat tax is unjustified and that exports should be resumed, otherwise Europe's image as a reliable supplier would be put at risk.
